title: Looks for floating-point expressions that can be expressed using built-in methods to improve both accuracy and performance.
summary: Negatively impacts accuracy and performance. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Lints for suspicious operations in impls of arithmetic operators, e.g. subtracting elements in an Add impl.
summary: This is probably a typo or copy-and-paste error and not intended. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of the non-existent =*, =! and =- operators.
summary: This is either a typo of *=, != or -= or confusing. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for Command::arg() invocations that look like they should be multiple arguments instead, such as arg("-t ext2").
summary: Command::arg() does not split arguments by space. An argument like arg("-t ext2") will be passed as a single argument to the command, which is likely not what was intended. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Detects the use of outer doc comments (///, /**) followed by a bang (!): ///!
summary: Triple-slash comments (known as “outer doc comments”) apply to items that follow it. An outer doc comment followed by a bang (i.e. ///!) has no specific meaning. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for formatting of else.
summary: It lints if the else is followed immediately by a newline or the else seems to be missing. This is probably some refactoring remnant, even if the code is correct, it might look confusing. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for calls to map followed by a count.
summary: It looks suspicious. Maybe map was confused with filter. If the map call is intentional, this should be rewritten using inspect. Or, if you intend to drive the iterator to completion, you can just use for_each instead. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Lints for suspicious operations in impls of OpAssign, e.g. subtracting elements in an AddAssign impl.
summary: This is probably a typo or copy-and-paste error and not intended. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for the suspicious use of OpenOptions::create() without an explicit OpenOptions::truncate().
summary: create() alone will either create a new file or open an existing file. If the file already exists, it will be overwritten when written to, but the file will not be truncated by default. If less data is written to the file than it already contains, the remainder of the file will remain unchanged, and the end of the file will contain old data. In most cases, one should either use create_new to ensure the file is created from scratch, or ensure truncate is called so that the truncation behaviour is explicit. truncate(true) will ensure the file is entirely overwritten with new data, whereas truncate(false) will explicitly keep the default behavior. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for unlikely usages of binary operators that are almost certainly typos and/or copy/paste errors, given the other usages of binary operators nearby.
summary: They are probably bugs and if they aren’t then they look like bugs and you should add a comment explaining why you are doing such an odd set of operations. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for calls to [splitn] (https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html#method.splitn) and related functions with either zero or one splits.
summary: These calls don’t actually split the value and are likely to be intended as a different number. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks for the usage of _.to_owned(), on a Cow<'_, _>.
summary: Calling to_owned() on a Cow creates a clone of the Cow itself, without taking ownership of the Cow contents (i.e. it’s equivalent to calling Cow::clone). The similarly named into_owned method, on the other hand, clones the Cow contents, effectively turning any Cow::Borrowed into a Cow::Owned. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks the formatting of a unary operator on the right hand side of a binary operator.
summary: It lints if there is no space between the binary and unary operators, but there is a space between the unary and its operand. This is either a typo in the binary operator or confusing. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Warns for a Bitwise XOR (^) operator being probably confused as a powering.
summary: It will not trigger if any of the numbers are not in decimal. It’s most probably a typo and may lead to unexpected behaviours. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.
